text:
alex: quick q — we turned on adaptive microbatch pacing on the rtx pool. curious best practice for measuring SLO vs throughput tradeoffs: do we rely on live-capture replay or run parameterized loadgen?

maria: my gut is replay for fidelity (kv patterns + burstiness), loadgen for controlled knobs. both needed.

jordan: agree. replay shows real kv-affinity spikes that break naive pacing. loadgen lets us sweep batch_size / pacing thresholds quickly.

emily: can we avoid full replay for every kernel change? replay is expensive. maybe a hybrid: replay for tail, synth for steady-state.

alex: that hybrid makes sense. curious about kernel selection — we saw kernel switch jitter when microbatch grows >8, p99 spikes. is that the runtime recompile/selection?

jordan: yes, that was kernel switch + cache eviction churn. timeline: increased microbatch -> larger seq peaks -> different kernel chosen -> KV cache misses increase -> p99 jump.

devon: this is why we need a metric that correlates kernel switches with tail events. bench-bot can we surface kernel-change counts in replay output?

bench-bot: posted results from last run 1987654200: 
```
run: hybrid-replay-2026-03-17
qps: 400
median: 18ms
p95: 62ms
p99: 210ms
kernel_switches: 47
kv_miss_rate: 12.6%
adaptive_batches_avg: 6.8
```

maria: 47 kernel switches per minute is high. suggests our kernel selection threshold is too sensitive to sequence-length variance. we should add hysteresis or sticky choice for X seconds.

emily: also see kv_miss_rate correlates with kernel_switches. when kernel changes, layout of kv slots moves -> cache warming. fixable with prefetch or preserve KV layout across kernel variants.

alex: concrete next steps? I propose: 1) run loadgen sweep (batch_size 1..12, pacing on/off) to map throughput curve; 2) run 1 replay focused on tail for top failing config; 3) instrument kernel-switch events in traces and add a flag to hold kernel for N seconds.

jordan: +1. for (1) use our param loadgen script: 
```
./loadgen --qps 200 --seq-dist heavy-tail.json --batch-max $B
```
we can parallelize B runs.

devon: and add a tiny eval set that captures KV hot prefixes so replay triggers realistic cache hits. reduces false negatives from totally random replay.

maria: we should also test p95 vs p99 sensitivity to sampling window. p95 may look fine while p99 dominated by cache-warm spikes. recommend reporting both and a 'kernel-change' annotated tail index.

alex: one more ops note — when doing loadgen, please set `use_opt_kernel=false` to baseline then flip to true for A/B. that isolates kernel perf delta from pacing.

bench-bot: scheduled jobs: loadgen-sweep-1987654300 (12 runs), replay-tail-1987654350 (1 run). will push raw traces to /bench/runs/1987654xxx.

emily: thanks. i'll prototype sticky-kernel patch and a small kv-preserve shim. will post perf diff in this thread.

jordan: if emily's patch reduces kernel_switches <10 and kv_miss_rate <5% under replay tail, we can relax pacing and reclaim throughput.

alex: perfect. ping here when results are in. :thumbsup:
